title: Jambalaya
subtitle: Louisiana Creole rice with chicken, andouille, and prawns
excerpt: The great one-pot dish of Louisiana: long-grain rice cooked directly in a richly spiced base of chicken, andouille sausage, and prawns with the holy trinity of Creole cooking until every grain is stained deep and flavoured through. No extra liquid added to serve.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jambalaya is the signature rice dish of Louisiana, drawing on the Spanish paella and the French influence in New Orleans Creole cooking, with additional contributions from West African rice traditions brought by enslaved people. The dish divides into two main camps: the Creole style (sometimes called red jambalaya) common in New Orleans, which includes tomatoes; and the Cajun style (brown jambalaya), made in the rural bayou country without tomatoes, where the colour comes from fond built by browning the meat. The essential ingredients are long-grain rice cooked in a well-seasoned broth, andouille sausage, and the Creole holy trinity of onion, celery, and green pepper. Prawns or crawfish are often added towards the end. The dish must not be stirred once the rice is in; stirring releases starch and makes the rice sticky and heavy rather than fluffy and separate.

content.text: Do not stir the rice once it goes into the pot. Press it down gently to submerge it and leave it alone until the liquid is absorbed. Stirring breaks the rice grains and releases starch, making the dish gluey. The rice should be fluffy and distinct. Use a heavy-based pot with a tight-fitting lid; a thin pot will scorch the bottom.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless; cut into 3 cm chunks

content.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over high heat. Season the chicken with salt. Brown the chicken pieces for 4 minutes per side until golden. Remove. Add the andouille and fry for 3 minutes until lightly browned. Remove. Reduce to medium heat. Add the onion, celery, and green pepper and cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, paprika, cayenne, thyme, and oregano and cook for 1 minute.

Return the chicken and andouille to the pot. Add the tinned tomatoes, chicken stock, and bay leaves. Bring to the boil. Add the rice and stir once to combine. Reduce to the lowest possible heat, cover tightly, and cook for 20 minutes without stirring.

Nestle the prawns into the surface of the rice, pressing them in slightly. Cover and cook for a further 5 to 7 minutes until the prawns are pink and the rice has absorbed all the liquid. Remove the bay leaves. Fluff gently with a fork. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter with spring onion and serve from the pot.
